liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **El Paso** (1 review, 1 other source): Garcia visibly struggles on El Paso, while the rest of the band plays fairly well; Weir played a dobro-like instrument on El Paso [2][8]
- **Cassidy** (2 reviews): Garcia gets badly lost during the Cassidy jam; Reviewer dislikes Cassidy as first-set closer; Garcia drifts in and out [5][12]
- **Rain** (1 review): Reviewer loves this Rain, recalling how Phil sounded especially good live [11]
- The Playing into Uncle John's Band segment is a standout of the strong second set [5]

## Setlist highlights

- **tunin' & teasin'**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [17]
- **tunin' & teasin'**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1995-02-20.145491.akg460b.lerond.t-flac1648** (recommended): source not stated; 21 songs; 161 min [1]
- **gd1995-02-20.144300.sbd.miller.clugston.flac1644**: soundboard; 20 songs; 152 min; rated 2.75/5 by 4 [2]
- **gd95-02-20.sbd.1297.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 143 min; rated 2.62/5 by 24 [3]. Said about its sound: Recording is very clean with no noticeable errors; its best feature; Sound quality is very good, apart from some buzzing; Reviewer likes the sound, which feels energetic from the first note [3][5][6][7][11][16]
- **gd1995-02-20.138045.set2.sbd.shnf**: soundboard; 11 songs; 83 min [4]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended these Salt Lake City shows as the last Grateful Dead concerts they ever saw [11]
- Lot vendors could have profited selling soda to caffeine-deprived Mormon youth instead of beer [14]
- Reviewer found the show flat and thought Garcia seemed tired from heavy touring [14]
- Entry to the Delta Center was very slow due to searches for caffeine and tobacco [15]
- Reviewer's group barely got in for Bertha into Greatest Story; this was their last Garcia show [15]
- Garcia flubs several lyrics, though the playing is fast and energetic [16]
- Weir played acoustic guitar on Little Red Rooster and Lazy River Road [2]
- First set ran 57 minutes and second set with encore ran 97 minutes [3]
- By the mid-1990s the band was largely carrying Garcia, reversing earlier roles [8]
- Reviewer says 1995 music quality had declined and this show falls short of a classic Day on the Green [9]
- The last night of the Salt Lake run is better than this one [12]
- Reviewer agrees the so-so reviews of this show are fairly accurate [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1995-02-20.145491.akg460b.lerond.t-flac1648**: taped by Jean Lerond; transferred by Jean Lerond; source: AKGC60B+CK8x shotgun in OTS, ~34’ to St.L of C (inline w/hanging PA; aimed at the PA) > Panasonic SV-255 (Paul Tumolo’s rig) Analog or Digi out, possibly via… [1]. Also: Recording is an audience taping made with AKG 460B microphones, attributed to Lerond [1]
- **gd1995-02-20.144300.sbd.miller.clugston.flac1644**: transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Master Soundboard Dat > 1st generation cassettes > Dat > HDD (.wav 16/44.1) [2]. Also: Soundboard source coordinated by Charlie Miller, with pitch correction assisted by Joe B. Jones [2]
- **gd95-02-20.sbd.1297.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > D > CD-R > EAC >SHN (note no cass gen) [3]. Also: Soundboard transferred via digital tape to CD-R, then EAC to SHN; via Brian Walker, mastered by Jay Serafin [3]
- **gd1995-02-20.138045.set2.sbd.shnf**: taped by unknown; transferred by Unknown; source: Set 2 Source: SBD > ? >SHN [4]. Also: This is a soundboard copy of set two only [4]
